title: CARE acadeME – Psychosocial Support and Advancement of the Nursing Programme during the Academic and Practical Work at the School of Nursing of the University Hospital Ulm
summary:
Training to become a nursing professional involves many challenges. Support needs arise due to varying educational backgrounds, language difficulties or personal stressors. At the same time, the demand for nursing professionals is constantly growing, which is why supporting a successful career path is so important.

The study examines which factors contribute to trainees successfully completing their training and how their positive professional motivation can be strengthened. It also examines reasons that promote a good working atmosphere and encourage long-term employment at the university hospital.

Data are collected with online-surveys, interviews and focus group discussions with all those involved in the training programme.
conditions: Psychological and physical demands related to academic and training work.

interventions.name: Trainee nursing professionals: participation in online surveys (T1 and T2) and focus group discussions.
Instructors (teachers, ward staff, practical instructors): participation in an online survey (T1) and focus group discussions.
Managers (Director of Nursing, Head of the Health Academy, Head of the Nursing School, Central Practical Instructors): Participation in individual interviews.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Trainee nursing staff at Ulm University Hospital; ward staff at Ulm University Hospital; central practical instructors and practical instructors; teaching staff at the nursing school; managers
Exclusion criteria:
None
